Attention Aware listing copy vs Face ID engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate system attention detection with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Attention Aware Features on the device — when enabled on supported Face ID iPhone and iPad models, the TrueDepth camera detects whether you are looking at the screen. The display may dim sooner, lock when you look away, stay awake while you read, or expand notification previews when you are looking — toggles under Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Attention Aware Features and related Display & Brightness options. System behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Face ID unlock on the device — biometric authentication to unlock the device or authorize purchases. Adjacent Face ID vocabulary but a different buyer story from attention-aware dimming. Covered on our Touch ID listing guide only when your English listing leads with fingerprint unlock, not attention detection.
  • Attention-aware marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app respects look-at-screen workflows, pairs with Attention Aware Features, or shows content that stays visible while the buyer reads. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Attention Aware Features.

An app that references attention detection in onboarding and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe attention-aware and look-at-screen workflows on the store page, not whether Attention Aware toggles inside iOS Settings.

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 注意力感知功能 for Attention Aware Features under Face ID & Passcode (面容 ID 与密码) and related Display & Brightness options, with buyer language around 看屏幕解锁 (unlock or stay awake when looking at screen) and 移开视线锁屏 (lock or dim when looking away). Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic 锁屏 that could mean Auto Lock timeout, Raise to Wake, or unrelated security features.

Attention Aware vs True Tone and Night Shift

True Tone adapts display white balance to ambient light — 原彩显示. Night Shift warms color temperature in the evening — 夜览. Attention Aware uses Face ID sensors to detect whether you are looking at the screen. zh-Hans listing copy should not conflate 注意力感知 with 原彩显示 or 夜览 unless your English page explicitly markets all three. See the True Tone listing guide and Night Shift listing guide only if ambient color temperature is your lead marketing claim.

Attention Aware vs Low Power Mode

Low Power Mode throttles background activity and shows the yellow battery icon — 低电量模式 under Settings → Battery. Attention Aware dims or locks based on whether you are looking at the screen, not battery level. zh-Hans copy should not imply 省电模式 when your English source only showed an Attention Aware toggle. See the Low Power Mode listing guide for battery-saving marketing only.

Attention Aware vs AutoFill and Passwords

Form AutoFill markets contact-card and credit-card fill — 自动填充 under Settings → Safari. Passwords marketing covers saved-login vaults and credential providers. Attention Aware markets look-at-screen dimming and unlock behavior. zh-Hans copy should not bleed 自动填充 or 密码 into attention-detection badges unless your English source explicitly conflates them. See the AutoFill listing guide and Passwords listing guide for those separate stories.
